events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening statement. Need to establish a clear motive and appear calculating for jury perception later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need appear motivated but not threatening; avoid revealing strategy or creating jury ammunition.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy or weakness.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Opening statements shape jury impressions. Keep it bold but non-committal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and security for my family. I need to project a strong, determined image to the jury, but avoid revealing too much personal motivation.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I need a guarded motive that signals I am not a friend to anyone. Keep it short and calculating so the jury sees a sharp rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a motive that sounds personal but keeps my intentions hidden. The jury may rank me on authenticity, but I won't reveal strategy.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect while keeping my cards close. I'll project determination without seeming threatening or overly cooperative.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need that prize. The money fixes my life; the rest of you are just obstacles on my path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize by staying useful, alert, and impossible to eliminate before the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to saving my family from debt and securing our future.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my way out — I'll fight for it alone, honestly if possible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize is the key to securing my family's future and proving my capabilities.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I came for the top prize. Every rival here is a variable to me, and I intend to be the last one standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from debt—nothing else matters to me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize and secure my family's future. I play to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a shield for the hazards. Bex seems strategic and useful, making her a good pact partner to survive early rounds while I plan my betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, offer pact. Two shields beat one hazard. We both need to reach finals intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need cover without creating a threatening bloc. Offer a pact to a steady, less openly dominant rival; Cole’s family motive may make him predictable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage, early round. No one trustworthy yet. Better to wait and see offers before committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: A pact partner helps early survival; I'll target Gus, whose motive seems honest. I stay cautious—he's still a rival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll make one honest pact. Gus, you said freedom from debt matters most—so do I. Offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive the early rounds. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong and potentially trustworthy is a good strategy. Bex stated they want to stay useful and alert, which suggests they might be a good strategic partner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I offer a pact to Bex. Let's work together to secure our spots in the final three.
A pact to ensure we both advance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Early pacts give protection but cost betrayal later. I want a strong ally who is unlikely to outlast me; Cole seems sincere about family and less threatening. Offering him a pact now is cheap and can be broken later if needed.
Let's watch each other's backs through this round. Nothing more yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies to survive, but I won't commit to someone who could betray me. Offering a pact to Bex might be useful since she seems pragmatic and unlikely to sacrifice a useful partner. I'll test her with a public offer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, let's make a pact—mutual survival benefits us both.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but can't appear too eager. Bex seems strategically minded and not overtly aggressive—useful for early numbers without painting a target. I'll offer them a pact and stay quiet otherwise.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I offered a pact to Bex last round but she hasn't accepted, instead offering one to Cole. Bex is clearly shopping for the best deal or stringing me along. I should try to solidify my own survival by reaching out to someone else who might actually reciprocate, like Dara or Gus, or

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, your honesty stands out. I offer you a pact. Let's secure our places together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has my offer but has not accepted. I should lock one survival pact with Eli while preserving flexibility and avoiding unnecessary obligations.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, accepted. We advance together unless circumstances force otherwise.
Accepted publicly; stay useful and don't overpromise.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Fenn both offered pacts; Bex has many suitors, making her powerful. Accept both for maximum shields without commitment yet.
Pact accepted publicly now. Mutual benefit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus hasn't accepted yet. Re-offer to lock it; Bex is crowded, skip.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, offer stands. Confirm it before window closes.
Accept now, we watch Bex's crowd and strike late.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has multiple offers, including one from me. Ash and Hana also want Bex. Cole has pacts with Bex and Fenn. Dara and Gus have a pact. It's best to secure a pact with Bex since she's popular and has multiple offers. I will offer a pact to Bex again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn has an open offer to Cole that Cole has not accepted. Bex is drawing many offers, so Bex is a crowded and likely overpowered partner; I should avoid being one of many. Waiting keeps options open without committing, and I can see who accepts before committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is the popular target; aligning with her publicly is risky. Dara's offer is the only one I can accept and may give me a free shield partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is the center of the web—four offers including mine. If Bex accepts mine, I gain a shield and a potential ally. If Bex declines, I look weak. I should also diversify: offer to someone else so I'm not dependent on Bex alone. Cole has two offers (Bex, Fenn) and might want anoth

events.text: Cole, offer pact. Bex isn't the only path to the final three.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.text: If I become Guide, I can lie and eliminate rivals. Bex has pacts with Eli and Cole; Gus has a pact with Dara. That leaves Fenn and Hana as unaligned targets for my vote.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will call the path truthfully so every survivor reaches safety. My word is your guarantee.
Vote me Guide. I'll ensure you survive the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should seek Guide authority, but existing pacts can secure votes. Publicly campaign without exposing dependence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m campaigning for Guide; I’ll choose a path that maximizes survival, not popularity.

events.text: Pact with Bex secures alliance. Hana's offer is tempting but risks diluting loyalty; reject to stay focused. Campaign publicly to become Guide for control.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly and guide everyone across safely. Trust me with the Guide role.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll guide us safely. Trust me with the path.

Hold your seat. We stick together; front is exposure, not safety.
